proof_summary: For odd \(m\) with \(\varphi(m)=2^{2^{33}}\), the totient product formula forces every prime factor to occur once and be a Fermat prime \(F_j\); the resulting sum of distinct \(2^j\)'s equals \(2^{33}\), so only \(j=33\) occurs and \(m=F_{33}\). Totient bounds—\(\varphi(m)<m\) for \(m>2\) and \(2\varphi(m)\le m\) for even \(m\)—then establish minimality, while any smaller odd candidate in the composite case would force \(\varphi(F_{33})=F_{33}-1\) and hence contradict compositeness.
